newsitem.title: FRANCE: Albanian author Kadare appeals for EU help.
newsitem.headline: Albanian author Kadare appeals for EU help.

text.p: Albania's best-known writer, Ismael Kadare, appealed on Friday to France and its European Union partners to help save his country from collapsing into anarchy and bloodshed.

Kadare, who has lived in Paris since he fled the then-Communist government in 1990, appealed to French President Jacques Chirac to take an initiative, saying only a European presence and arbitration could save Albania from genocide.

"In these conditions of terror, I believe it is necessary to have international arbitration, even a symbolic presence. It is urgent because there could be a castastrophe, even genocide, this weekend," Kadare told Europe 1 radio.

Embattled President Sali Berisha and all the Balkan state's political parties appealed on Thursday to European NATO members to send peacekeepers to restore order as anarchy spread across Albania with protesters looting weapons from army barracks.

Kadare, author of acclaimed novels such as "The General of the Dead Army" and "The Concert", said that Albanians watching foreign governments evacuate their nationals felt their country was being abandoned to its fate, as it had been during the Stalinist dictatorship of the late Enver Hoxha.

"It adds to the feeling of abandonment we had for 45 years," he said, stressing that Albania was a European country bordering on European Union member Greece and a mere 100 km (60 miles) by sea from Italy.

"I am not a politician...but I just want to express my wish that the French president take an initiative. It's a country where French is spoken. France could act with the help of the British, the Germans and above all the Italians," he said.

German Chancellor Helmut Kohl made clear after talks with the current president of the EU, Dutch Prime Minister Wim Kok, on Thursday that he saw the crisis in Albania as internal and saw no role for outside peacekeepers.

Chirac is travelling in Latin America and in his absence, French officials have kept a low profile on the Albania crisis, stressing international political mediation efforts with no mention of possible military action.
